stem: A 9-month-old Aboriginal infant from a remote community is brought to clinic with fever, irritability, and repeated ear tugging; which statement best guides the assessment?

options.text: Ear tugging may be the only sign of ear pain in an infant, so acute otitis media should still be considered
Acute otitis media is usually bacterial, so viral causes are unlikely
Pseudomonas is the usual organism in uncomplicated acute otitis media
A diagnosis of acute otitis media does not require acute symptoms if the child is at risk of later language delay
Otitis media in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children is mainly a school-age problem rather than an infant problem

explanation: Ear tugging may be the only sign of ear pain in an infant, so acute otitis media should still be considered. In infants and toddlers, symptoms can be non-specific, and ear tugging may be the only clue to middle ear infection. Diagnosis still requires acute onset of signs and symptoms of acute middle ear infection, and otitis media is an important problem in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and may occur earlier.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because infants may not be able to describe ear pain, and ear tugging can be the only sign that acute otitis media should be considered
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because acute otitis media is usually viral rather than bacterial
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Pseudomonas is not the usual organism in uncomplicated acute otitis media; the common pathogens are Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because diagnosis of acute otitis media still requires acute onset of signs and symptoms of middle ear infection
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because otitis media can occur earlier in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and is not mainly a school-age problem
